name: Superposition
fallback_description: Superposition lets a quantum state exist as a weighted combination of basis states, which is what gives quantum algorithms their interference-based power.

steps.title: Prepare a basis state
steps.description: A qubit usually starts in a definite state like |0>. That gives us a clear reference point before any quantum evolution happens.

steps.title: Apply a mixing gate
steps.description: A gate such as the Hadamard rotates the qubit into a combination of |0> and |1>. The state now carries amplitudes for multiple outcomes at once.

steps.title: Preserve amplitudes coherently
steps.description: While the system stays isolated, the amplitudes evolve together and can later reinforce or cancel one another. That coherent evolution is what algorithms exploit.

steps.title: Measure to get one outcome
steps.description: When you finally measure, the superposition collapses to one classical result. The algorithm's job is to shape the amplitudes so the useful result is the most likely one.

name: Quantum Gates
fallback_description: Quantum gates are reversible operations that change amplitudes and phases on one or more qubits, forming the building blocks of quantum circuits.

steps.title: Represent the state
steps.description: A qubit or register is described by amplitudes rather than a single classical bit value. Gates act directly on that state description.

steps.title: Apply a unitary operation
steps.description: Each gate is a mathematically reversible transformation that rotates or entangles amplitudes without losing information.

steps.title: Compose gates into circuits
steps.description: Useful algorithms come from chaining many simple gates together. The ordering matters because each step changes the state the next gate sees.

steps.title: Measure at the end
steps.description: After the gate sequence has shaped the amplitudes, a measurement turns the quantum state into a classical answer.

name: Measurement
fallback_description: Measurement converts a quantum state into a classical outcome, with probabilities determined by the state's amplitudes in the chosen basis.

steps.title: Choose a basis
steps.description: A measurement is always made with respect to some basis, such as the computational basis or an alternative rotated basis.

steps.title: Sample according to amplitudes
steps.description: The probability of each possible result is determined by the squared magnitude of its amplitude in that basis.

steps.title: Collapse the state
steps.description: Once measured, the system is projected onto the observed outcome. The original superposition is no longer available afterward.

name: Oracle
fallback_description: A quantum oracle is a black-box subroutine that encodes a function into a reversible operation, allowing the algorithm to query hidden structure coherently.

steps.title: Encode a hidden function
steps.description: The oracle represents information the algorithm wants to learn, such as whether a function is balanced or which item is marked.

steps.title: Act coherently on superpositions
steps.description: Instead of querying one classical input at a time, the oracle acts on a superposition of inputs in a single quantum step.

steps.title: Expose structure through interference
steps.description: The rest of the circuit turns the phase or amplitude patterns left by the oracle into a measurable signature.

name: Interference
fallback_description: Interference is the process by which amplitudes combine, sometimes reinforcing useful outcomes and sometimes canceling unwanted ones.

steps.title: Create multiple paths
steps.description: Superposition gives the computation several amplitude paths to evolve at once.

steps.title: Adjust relative phases
steps.description: Gates and oracles change the sign or angle of amplitudes, setting up how those paths will combine.

steps.title: Recombine the paths
steps.description: Later gates bring amplitudes back together so the right answers grow stronger while the wrong ones shrink.

name: Entanglement
fallback_description: Entanglement creates correlations between qubits that cannot be explained by independent classical states, making distributed quantum effects possible.

steps.title: Prepare correlated qubits
steps.description: A circuit such as Hadamard plus CNOT creates a joint state that cannot be factored into separate single-qubit states.

steps.title: Manipulate the joint system
steps.description: Operations on one part of the entangled state affect the full register description, not just one isolated qubit.

steps.title: Use correlations operationally
steps.description: Protocols like teleportation and superdense coding rely on these correlations to move information in ways classical systems cannot.

name: Phase Kickback
fallback_description: Phase kickback is the trick where a controlled operation writes useful information into the phase of a control qubit instead of only into a target qubit.

steps.title: Set up a control-target pair
steps.description: A control qubit interacts with a target prepared so that the target's response can be reflected back as a phase.

steps.title: Apply the controlled operation
steps.description: The controlled unitary changes the global state in a way that depends on the control value and target structure.

steps.title: Read out the phase indirectly
steps.description: Later interference steps reveal the phase pattern as a measurable classical result.

name: Hadamard Transform
fallback_description: The Hadamard transform spreads a basis state across multiple amplitudes and is one of the main ways quantum circuits enter and exit interference patterns.

steps.title: Start in a basis state
steps.description: A qubit begins in |0> or |1>, which is easy to prepare and reason about.

steps.title: Apply the Hadamard gate
steps.description: The gate maps that state into an equal superposition, differing only by phase depending on the starting value.

steps.title: Use repeated Hadamards strategically
steps.description: Many algorithms apply Hadamards both before and after an oracle so hidden phase information can be converted into readable amplitudes.

name: Amplitude Amplification
fallback_description: Amplitude amplification boosts the probability of desired outcomes by repeatedly marking good states and reflecting amplitudes about their average.

steps.title: Prepare a broad superposition
steps.description: The register begins spread across many candidate answers so the target is present with small initial weight.

steps.title: Mark good states
steps.description: An oracle flips the phase of the desired state or states without explicitly revealing them.

steps.title: Reflect about the mean
steps.description: The diffusion step redistributes amplitudes so marked states gain probability while unmarked ones lose some.

name: Phase Rotation
fallback_description: Phase rotations adjust the angle of amplitudes without necessarily changing measurement probabilities immediately, which makes them crucial for interference and Fourier-style circuits.

steps.title: Target a specific amplitude component
steps.description: A phase gate changes the relative angle of one part of the state with respect to another.

steps.title: Preserve probability magnitudes
steps.description: The state can look unchanged to a direct measurement at that moment because the amplitudes' magnitudes stay the same.

steps.title: Reveal the phase later
steps.description: Subsequent interference converts those hidden phase differences into visible probability shifts.

name: Controlled Unitary
fallback_description: A controlled unitary applies an operation only when a control qubit is in the right state, letting circuits build conditional logic while remaining reversible.

steps.title: Choose a control qubit
steps.description: One qubit determines whether the operation should happen or not.

steps.title: Conditionally apply the target gate
steps.description: If the control is active, the unitary is applied to the target register; otherwise the target is left alone.

steps.title: Use it to encode structure
steps.description: Controlled operations are central in entanglement, phase estimation, oracles, and many deeper algorithms.

name: Ancilla Qubit
fallback_description: An ancilla qubit is a helper qubit introduced to store temporary information, assist reversible computation, or make measurements indirect.

steps.title: Add workspace to the circuit
steps.description: Ancillas give the circuit extra room to compute intermediate values without overwriting useful information.

steps.title: Use the helper during computation
steps.description: The ancilla may collect phase information, hold syndromes, or support reversible subroutines.

steps.title: Uncompute or measure it carefully
steps.description: Good circuits either return ancillas to a clean state or measure them in a way that preserves the main computation's meaning.

name: Amplitude Encoding
fallback_description: Amplitude encoding stores classical data in the amplitudes of a quantum state, allowing algorithms to compare or process vectors in quantum form.

steps.title: Normalize the data
steps.description: A classical vector must first be scaled so it can represent a valid quantum state's amplitudes.

steps.title: Prepare the state
steps.description: The circuit loads that vector into a register, which is often one of the hardest parts of a practical quantum ML routine.

steps.title: Process overlaps and features
steps.description: Once encoded, the state can be compared or transformed using quantum operations suited to similarity estimation or learning tasks.

name: Variational Circuit
fallback_description: A variational circuit is a parameterized quantum circuit whose angles are tuned by a classical optimizer to minimize or maximize an objective.

steps.title: Choose a parameterized ansatz
steps.description: The circuit structure includes tunable rotation angles that define a family of candidate quantum states.

steps.title: Measure an objective
steps.description: For each parameter setting, the quantum computer estimates a cost such as energy, classification loss, or cut value.

steps.title: Update parameters classically
steps.description: A classical optimizer proposes better parameters and the loop repeats until the objective improves enough.

name: Error Correction
fallback_description: Quantum error correction protects fragile quantum information by encoding logical states across multiple physical qubits and extracting syndromes without directly measuring the state.

steps.title: Encode redundancy
steps.description: Logical information is spread across multiple qubits so that single physical faults do not destroy the message.

steps.title: Measure syndromes indirectly
steps.description: Auxiliary checks reveal which kind of error likely happened without exposing the protected logical amplitudes.

steps.title: Apply a correction
steps.description: Based on the syndrome, the circuit or controller reverses the inferred error and restores the logical state.

name: Bell Pair
fallback_description: A Bell pair is a maximally entangled two-qubit state used as a standard resource for teleportation, superdense coding, and distributed quantum protocols.

steps.title: Prepare two clean qubits
steps.description: Both qubits typically begin in simple basis states so the entangling operation has a known starting point.

steps.title: Entangle them with H and CNOT
steps.description: A Hadamard on one qubit followed by a controlled-NOT creates a correlated state such as (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2).

steps.title: Use the pair as a resource
steps.description: Once distributed, the Bell pair enables tasks that require nonclassical shared correlations between distant parties.

name: Classical Communication
fallback_description: Many quantum protocols still need ordinary classical messages to complete coordination, apply corrections, or compare measurement choices.

steps.title: Extract a classical bit string
steps.description: A measurement outcome or control decision is converted into ordinary classical information.

steps.title: Send the message over a normal channel
steps.description: That information can be copied, stored, and transmitted using standard communication methods.

steps.title: Finish the protocol with corrections
steps.description: The receiving party uses the classical message to choose a recovery, comparison, or next protocol step.

name: Deutsch Algorithm
fallback_description: Deutsch's algorithm distinguishes constant and balanced single-bit Boolean oracles with one quantum query by combining phase kickback with interference.

templates.constant-0:
NOTE Deutsch Algorithm - constant-0 oracle

INIT q0
INIT q1 1
H q0
H q1

LABEL Oracle: f(x)=0
NOTE No oracle action needed

LABEL Final interference
H q0
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z
templates.constant-1:
NOTE Deutsch Algorithm - constant-1 oracle

INIT q0
INIT q1 1
H q0
H q1

LABEL Oracle: f(x)=1
X q1

LABEL Final interference
H q0
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z
templates.balanced:
NOTE Deutsch Algorithm - balanced oracle

INIT q0
INIT q1 1
H q0
H q1

LABEL Oracle: f(x)=x
CNOT q0 q1

LABEL Final interference
H q0
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z

steps.title: Prepare the input and ancilla
steps.description: Start with one query qubit and one helper qubit, then apply Hadamard gates so the circuit can evaluate both possible inputs coherently.

steps.title: Call the oracle once
steps.description: The oracle acts on the superposed input and writes information about the hidden function into the phase of the state.

steps.title: Interfere the amplitudes
steps.description: A final Hadamard on the query qubit turns the hidden phase pattern into a measurable classical signal.

steps.title: Read the result
steps.description: Measuring the query qubit tells you whether the oracle was constant or balanced after only one query.

name: Deutsch-Jozsa Algorithm
fallback_description: Deutsch-Jozsa generalizes the Deutsch setting to n-bit oracles, deciding whether a promised function is constant or balanced with a single coherent query.
complexity: O(1) oracle query under the promise

templates.2-constant:
NOTE Deutsch-Jozsa - 2 input qubits, constant oracle

INIT q0
INIT q1
INIT q2 1
H q0
H q1
H q2

LABEL Oracle: constant
NOTE No controlled flips

H q0
H q1
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z
MEASURE q1 BASIS Z

H q2

CNOT q1 q2

H q0
H q1
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z
MEASURE q1 BASIS Z

steps.title: Create a superposition over inputs
steps.description: Apply Hadamard gates to all query qubits so the oracle sees every possible input at once.

steps.title: Use an ancilla to capture phase
steps.description: The helper qubit is prepared so the oracle's effect is written into phase rather than only into output bits.

steps.title: Apply the oracle once
steps.description: The balanced-versus-constant structure changes the phase pattern across the input register in one coherent query.

steps.title: Undo with Hadamards and measure
steps.description: A second layer of Hadamards converts that phase pattern into a simple measurement signature: all zeros or not.

name: Bernstein-Vazirani Algorithm
fallback_description: Bernstein-Vazirani recovers a hidden bit string in one oracle call by encoding the secret into relative phases and decoding it with Hadamard interference.

steps.title: Prepare the query register
steps.description: All input qubits are placed into superposition so they can probe every relevant bit pattern simultaneously.

steps.title: Apply the hidden-string oracle
steps.description: The oracle uses phase kickback so the secret string is imprinted into the phase structure of the input register.

steps.title: Run Hadamards again
steps.description: The second Hadamard layer decodes the phase pattern directly into the computational basis.

steps.title: Measure the full string
steps.description: One measurement of the register reveals the hidden bit string in a single query.

name: Simon's Algorithm
fallback_description: Simon's algorithm samples linear equations orthogonal to a hidden xor mask and solves them classically, giving an exponential separation over brute-force search.

templates.2:
NOTE Simon's Algorithm - 2-qubit hidden period example

INIT q0
INIT q1
INIT q2
INIT q3

LABEL Superpose input register
H q0
H q1

LABEL Oracle with hidden period s=11
CNOT q0 q2
CNOT q1 q3
CNOT q0 q3
CNOT q1 q2

MEASURE q2 BASIS Z
MEASURE q3 BASIS Z
H q0
H q1
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z
MEASURE q1 BASIS Z
templates.3:
NOTE Simon's Algorithm - 3-qubit hidden period example

INIT q0
INIT q1
INIT q2
INIT q3
INIT q4
INIT q5

LABEL Superpose input register
H q0
H q1
H q2

LABEL Oracle with hidden period s=101
CNOT q0 q3
CNOT q1 q4
CNOT q2 q5
CNOT q0 q5
CNOT q2 q3

MEASURE q3 BASIS Z
MEASURE q4 BASIS Z
MEASURE q5 BASIS Z
H q0
H q1
H q2
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z
MEASURE q1 BASIS Z
MEASURE q2 BASIS Z

steps.title: Superpose all candidate inputs
steps.description: The input register is spread over every possible bit string so the oracle can act on them together.

steps.title: Query the two-to-one oracle
steps.description: The oracle maps paired inputs with the same hidden xor relation to the same output state.

steps.title: Measure the output register
steps.description: That measurement leaves the input register in a structured superposition tied to the hidden period.

steps.title: Collect equations from repeated runs
steps.description: After another interference step and measurement, each run yields a linear constraint that helps recover the secret string.

name: Grover's Search
fallback_description: Grover's search alternates oracle phase marking with diffusion to amplify a target basis state, reducing unstructured search from linear to square-root query complexity.

steps.title: Initialize a uniform search state
steps.description: Hadamard gates spread amplitude equally across all candidate answers in the search space.

steps.title: Mark the target with the oracle
steps.description: The oracle flips the phase of the desired state without directly revealing which one it is.

steps.title: Apply the diffusion operator
steps.description: A reflection about the average amplitude boosts the marked state while slightly reducing the rest.

steps.title: Repeat and then measure
steps.description: After enough iterations, the target state's probability becomes high enough that a final measurement likely returns it.

name: Quantum Fourier Transform
fallback_description: The quantum Fourier transform applies structured phase rotations and swaps to map computational-basis amplitudes into the frequency domain with polylogarithmic depth.
complexity: O(n^2) gates in the standard circuit

templates.2:
NOTE 2-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform

INIT q0 1
INIT q1

H q0
CNOT q1 q0
RZ q0 -1.5708
CNOT q1 q0
RZ q0 1.5708
H q1
SWAP q0 q1
templates.3:
NOTE 3-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform

INIT q0 1
INIT q1
INIT q2

H q0
CNOT q1 q0
RZ q0 -1.5708
CNOT q1 q0
RZ q0 1.5708
CNOT q2 q0
RZ q0 -0.7854
CNOT q2 q0
RZ q0 0.7854
H q1
CNOT q2 q1
RZ q1 -1.5708
CNOT q2 q1
RZ q1 1.5708
H q2
SWAP q0 q2
templates.4:
NOTE 4-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform

INIT q0 1
INIT q1
INIT q2
INIT q3

H q0
CNOT q1 q0
RZ q0 -1.5708
CNOT q1 q0
RZ q0 1.5708
CNOT q2 q0
RZ q0 -0.7854
CNOT q2 q0
RZ q0 0.7854
CNOT q3 q0
RZ q0 -0.3927
CNOT q3 q0
RZ q0 0.3927
H q1
CNOT q2 q1
RZ q1 -1.5708
CNOT q2 q1
RZ q1 1.5708
CNOT q3 q1
RZ q1 -0.7854
CNOT q3 q1
RZ q1 0.7854
H q2
CNOT q3 q2
RZ q2 -1.5708
CNOT q3 q2
RZ q2 1.5708
H q3
SWAP q0 q3
SWAP q1 q2

steps.title: Start with an encoded register
steps.description: The input register holds amplitudes or phases that represent the signal or computational pattern you want to transform.

steps.title: Apply layered Hadamards and controlled phases
steps.description: Each qubit receives a Hadamard and conditional phase rotations that accumulate frequency-style information from the lower-order qubits.

steps.title: Reverse qubit order with swaps
steps.description: A final bit-reversal step restores the conventional ordering of the transformed output register.

steps.title: Use the transformed state downstream
steps.description: The result is often not measured immediately but fed into larger algorithms such as phase estimation or period finding.

name: Quantum Phase Estimation
fallback_description: Quantum phase estimation extracts eigenphases by coupling a target unitary to an estimation register and decoding the phase pattern with the inverse quantum Fourier transform.
complexity: Polynomial in precision and controlled-unitary cost

steps.title: Prepare estimation qubits and an eigenstate
steps.description: One register is set up to record the phase while another holds a state that responds predictably to the chosen unitary.

steps.title: Apply controlled powers of the unitary
steps.description: Each estimation qubit controls a different power of the unitary, building a binary representation of the phase into the system.

steps.title: Run the inverse QFT
steps.description: The inverse quantum Fourier transform reorganizes the phase information into readable basis-state amplitudes.

steps.title: Measure the estimation register
steps.description: The measurement returns a bit string that approximates the eigenphase.

name: Shor's Algorithm - Factorization
fallback_description: Shor's algorithm reduces integer factorization to order finding, pairing modular arithmetic with quantum period finding for exponential asymptotic speedup over classical factoring.

steps.title: Reduce factoring to period finding
steps.description: The algorithm reformulates the factoring problem so that finding a modular period is the central quantum task.

steps.title: Build a periodic quantum state
steps.description: A superposition of exponents and modular arithmetic create a state whose structure repeats with the hidden order.

steps.title: Extract the period with QFT-style interference
steps.description: A Fourier-based readout turns the periodic pattern into peaks that reveal the order information.

steps.title: Finish classically
steps.description: Classical number theory uses the recovered order to derive nontrivial factors of the integer.

name: HHL Algorithm
fallback_description: The HHL algorithm solves certain sparse linear systems by encoding the solution into a quantum state using phase estimation, controlled rotations, and uncomputation.
complexity: Polylogarithmic in dimension under strong assumptions

steps.title: Encode the right-hand-side vector
steps.description: The input vector is loaded into a quantum state so the system of equations is represented in amplitude form.

steps.title: Estimate eigenvalues
steps.description: Phase estimation approximates the matrix's eigenvalue information on a helper register.

steps.title: Apply controlled inversion logic
steps.description: A controlled rotation uses those estimated eigenvalues to weight amplitudes by inverse eigenvalue factors.

steps.title: Uncompute and measure
steps.description: After removing temporary information, the remaining quantum state encodes the solution up to normalization.

name: QSVM Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum support vector machines use quantum feature maps or kernel estimation routines to classify data in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
complexity: Varies by feature map and kernel estimation cost

steps.title: Encode the input data
steps.description: Classical features are embedded into quantum states using a chosen feature map or amplitude encoding routine.

steps.title: Estimate kernel similarity
steps.description: The circuit measures overlaps between encoded states to build a quantum-informed notion of similarity.

steps.title: Train or evaluate the classifier
steps.description: Those similarities are used inside a support-vector-style decision boundary to separate labeled examples.

name: QKmean Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum k-means variants use overlap estimation, swap tests, or amplitude encodings to accelerate distance evaluation in clustering workflows.
complexity: Depends on state preparation and distance routine

steps.title: Encode data points and centroids
steps.description: Both samples and candidate cluster centers are represented as quantum states.

steps.title: Estimate similarity or distance
steps.description: The circuit uses a quantum subroutine to compare each sample against available centroids.

steps.title: Update cluster assignments
steps.description: Based on those comparisons, the algorithm reassigns samples and updates the centroids iteratively.

name: QKNN Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum nearest-neighbor methods use encoded feature states and quantum similarity estimation to compare data points for classification.
complexity: Depends on encoding and similarity oracle cost

steps.title: Prepare the query and reference states
steps.description: The unknown sample and stored training examples are loaded into quantum representations.

steps.title: Estimate pairwise similarity
steps.description: A quantum subroutine measures how close the query is to each candidate neighbor.

steps.title: Vote from the nearest results
steps.description: The closest matches determine the label or category assigned to the query sample.

name: QHC Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum hierarchical clustering approaches estimate pairwise similarities in encoded spaces to build dendrogram-style cluster structures.
complexity: Driven by similarity estimation and merge schedule

steps.title: Encode the dataset
steps.description: Each data point is mapped into a quantum state that can be compared against the others.

steps.title: Compute pairwise closeness
steps.description: Quantum similarity routines estimate which clusters or points should merge first.

steps.title: Build the hierarchy
steps.description: The clustering tree is assembled by repeatedly merging the most similar groups.

name: QPCA Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum PCA extracts dominant eigencomponents of a density operator or covariance-like object using phase-estimation-style primitives.
complexity: Depends on access model to the density operator

steps.title: Represent the covariance-like object
steps.description: The dataset must be available in a form that the quantum routine can treat like a density operator or matrix.

steps.title: Use phase-estimation machinery
steps.description: Eigenvalue and eigenvector information is extracted with a phase-estimation-style procedure.

steps.title: Interpret dominant components
steps.description: The largest components describe the principal structure of the data, similar to classical PCA.

name: QPerceptron Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum perceptron models adapt thresholded learning ideas to parameterized quantum circuits and measurement-based outputs.
complexity: Training cost depends on ansatz and optimizer

steps.title: Encode inputs into a circuit
steps.description: Features are mapped into a small quantum register using a chosen embedding.

steps.title: Apply trainable transformations
steps.description: Parameterized gates act like learnable weights, changing the quantum state's orientation.

steps.title: Measure and threshold the output
steps.description: The measured signal is interpreted as a binary or class decision and compared with the target label.

name: QNN Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum neural networks use trainable parameterized circuits as differentiable models for classification, regression, and generative learning.
complexity: Training cost depends on circuit depth and optimization loop

steps.title: Embed the input data
steps.description: Classical features are first encoded into a quantum state the network can process.

steps.title: Run parameterized layers
steps.description: Trainable rotations and entangling gates act like the learnable layers of a classical neural model.

steps.title: Measure and optimize
steps.description: Measurements produce outputs that are scored by a loss function, and a classical optimizer tunes the parameters.

name: QAOA MaxCut
fallback_description: QAOA alternates cost and mixer layers to variationally optimize combinatorial objectives, with MaxCut as a standard benchmark problem.
complexity: Depends on depth p and optimization budget

steps.title: Prepare a uniform starting state
steps.description: The qubits begin in a superposition that represents all candidate cut assignments at once.

steps.title: Apply a cost layer
steps.description: Problem-specific phase rotations reward assignments that satisfy more of the target objective.

steps.title: Apply a mixer layer
steps.description: A second set of gates redistributes amplitudes so the algorithm can continue exploring new assignments.

steps.title: Optimize the angles
steps.description: A classical outer loop tunes the layer parameters until high-quality cuts become likely at measurement.

name: VQE Ansatz (H2 molecule)
fallback_description: Variational quantum eigensolvers estimate molecular ground-state energies by preparing an ansatz, measuring Hamiltonian terms, and optimizing parameters classically.
complexity: Hybrid iterative optimization with repeated measurements

steps.title: Choose an ansatz for the molecule
steps.description: A parameterized circuit defines the family of candidate states used to approximate the molecule's ground state.

steps.title: Measure the Hamiltonian expectation
steps.description: The circuit is executed many times to estimate the energy contributed by the molecule's terms.

steps.title: Update parameters classically
steps.description: A classical optimizer searches for parameter values that minimize the measured energy.

name: Quantum Walk (1D)
fallback_description: Discrete-time quantum walks use a coin-plus-shift construction to spread amplitudes ballistically across a graph or line.
complexity: Linear in walk depth for the simulated circuit

steps.title: Prepare a coin and position register
steps.description: One part of the state chooses direction while the rest tracks where the walker is on the line.

steps.title: Flip the coin into superposition
steps.description: The coin qubit is mixed so the walker can move left and right at the same time.

steps.title: Shift conditionally on the coin
steps.description: A conditional move entangles direction with position and spreads the walk across the graph.

steps.title: Repeat to build the distribution
steps.description: Multiple rounds produce a sharply structured probability pattern shaped by quantum interference.

name: QEC: 3-Qubit Repetition Code
arxiv_query: three qubit repetition code quantum error correction
fallback_description: The three-qubit repetition code protects against single bit-flip errors using redundancy, syndrome extraction, and corrective decoding.
complexity: Constant-size encoding for single bit-flip correction

steps.title: Encode one logical bit into three qubits
steps.description: Redundancy spreads the logical information across three physical lines.

steps.title: Detect a mismatch with syndromes
steps.description: Parity-style checks reveal whether one qubit has likely flipped without directly reading the logical state.

steps.title: Correct the identified error
steps.description: Once the failing line is known, a targeted bit flip restores the encoded logical value.

name: QEC: Shor's Nine-Qubit Code
fallback_description: Shor's nine-qubit code combines repetition in complementary bases to correct arbitrary single-qubit bit-flip and phase-flip errors.
complexity: Constant-size code for arbitrary single-qubit error correction

steps.title: Nest repetition across two bases
steps.description: The code protects against both bit flips and phase flips by combining different redundancy patterns.

steps.title: Extract multiple syndromes
steps.description: Separate checks identify which type of error happened and where it occurred.

steps.title: Apply the corresponding recovery
steps.description: With the syndrome information in hand, the code reverses the single-qubit error and restores the logical state.

name: BB84 With Eve
fallback_description: BB84 is a prepare-and-measure key distribution protocol where basis mismatch statistics reveal eavesdropping through an elevated quantum bit error rate.

templates.base:
NOTE BB84 protocol - {{KEY_LENGTH}} rounds

ACTOR Alice
ACTOR Bob
ACTOR Eve

LABEL Shared setup
NOTE Repeat the following workflow for {{KEY_LENGTH}} rounds

LABEL Example round
INIT q0 +
ASSIGN q0 Alice
SEND q0 Alice Bob
INTERCEPT q0 Eve
SEND q0 Eve Bob
MEASURE q0 BASIS Z

NOTE Basis comparison and key sifting happen after transmission

steps.title: Alice prepares random bits and bases
steps.description: Each transmitted qubit is encoded using one of two possible bases so an eavesdropper cannot copy it safely.

steps.title: Bob measures in random bases
steps.description: Bob receives each qubit and chooses his measurement basis independently, which means some rounds will match Alice and some will not.

steps.title: They sift matching rounds
steps.description: Alice and Bob publicly compare only the bases, keeping the rounds where they happened to match.

steps.title: They estimate the error rate
steps.description: If Eve disturbed too many qubits, the sifted key shows too many errors and the protocol is aborted.

name: Teleportation Walkthrough
fallback_description: Quantum teleportation transfers an unknown qubit state using a shared entangled pair, a Bell-basis measurement, and two classical correction bits.

steps.title: Share an entangled Bell pair
steps.description: Alice and Bob begin by holding one qubit each from a previously prepared entangled pair.

steps.title: Entangle the message with Alice's half
steps.description: Alice combines the unknown state with her Bell-pair qubit and performs a Bell-basis style measurement.

steps.title: Send two classical bits
steps.description: The measurement outcome is ordinary classical information, so Alice can transmit it over a normal channel.

steps.title: Bob applies the recovery
steps.description: Using those two bits, Bob chooses the right correction gate and reconstructs the original unknown state on his qubit.

name: Superdense Coding
fallback_description: Superdense coding uses a shared Bell pair so that one transmitted qubit can communicate two classical bits after an entangling decode.

steps.title: Share an entangled pair
steps.description: Alice and Bob first hold opposite halves of a Bell pair that acts as a communication resource.

steps.title: Encode two classical bits locally
steps.description: Alice applies one of four possible gate patterns to her qubit, choosing an operation that represents the message.

steps.title: Send one qubit to Bob
steps.description: Only Alice's single qubit is transmitted, while the shared entanglement carries the extra structure.

steps.title: Decode with a joint measurement
steps.description: Bob performs the right two-qubit operations and measurements to recover both classical bits.

name: N-Qubit Teleportation
fallback_description: Multi-qubit teleportation extends the standard protocol by teleporting each component through coordinated entanglement resources and classical corrections.
complexity: Scales with payload qubits and Bell channels

steps.title: Prepare one Bell channel per payload qubit
steps.description: Each qubit in the message needs matching entanglement resources so the full register can be transferred safely.

steps.title: Measure each payload with its local channel
steps.description: Alice performs teleportation-style operations for every qubit she wants to move.

steps.title: Send the classical correction data
steps.description: The measurement results are transmitted so Bob knows how to recover each teleported qubit.

steps.title: Reassemble the full register
steps.description: Bob applies the required corrections across all received qubits, reconstructing the multi-qubit state.

name: Veto Algorithm
fallback_description: Quantum veto protocols let one or more participants anonymously block a shared decision using entanglement-assisted multiparty coordination.
complexity: Multiparty protocol with shared entanglement rounds

steps.title: Distribute shared quantum resources
steps.description: Participants begin with correlated quantum states that encode group-wide information without revealing personal choices yet.

steps.title: Let each participant act privately
steps.description: Anyone who wants to veto applies a local operation, while others follow the neutral branch of the protocol.

steps.title: Collect a joint outcome
steps.description: A shared measurement or comparison step reveals whether any veto occurred without exposing who applied it.

name: QPC (Socialist Millionaire)
fallback_description: Quantum private comparison protocols allow parties to compare secrets, such as equality, without revealing the secrets themselves.
complexity: Secure comparison with communication and verification rounds

steps.title: Encode private values indirectly
steps.description: Each party contributes information to the protocol without sending the secret itself in plain classical form.

steps.title: Use shared quantum correlations and checks
steps.description: Quantum states and measurements let the protocol detect agreement or mismatch while limiting information leakage.

steps.title: Reveal only the comparison result
steps.description: At the end, the parties learn whether the values match, but not the values themselves.
